doc.title: Qualified Variables
doc.paragraph: Adaptive Script allows you to declare local and const variables, using the let and const keywords.

Some variables are declared outside of the execution a script, expression or template. These variables are read-only and are provided by Adaptive Framework, often to share contextual information that may be useful for developer when trying to rendering a decision. For example, Adaptive Models often evaluate adaptive scripts in order to transform objects and properties. In order to do so, the script, may need to obtain access to the properties or values that they are in the process of transforming. These special, read-only variables are called Qualified Variables.

Qualified Variables take the form qualifier::identifier. The qualifier part of the variable is derived from the context in which the variable is provided. For instance, current::mappedObjectTypeId is a Qualified Variable that is provided by the Adaptive Models when processing an object that is being mapped to another object.

Application conf may define qualified variables under qualifiedVariables using template strings. Those templates are compiled when the application conf is loaded (or reloaded). Compile-time substitutions (#{…}) run at load time and freeze a value for that config; evaluation-time substitutions (${…}) re-run each time the variable is evaluated. See Templates and Expressions for details.

For debugging and tooling, qualifier(name) returns a fresh object whose properties are the variables for that qualifier on the current execution context stack (issue #9). Each call builds a new object; it is not a live proxy. All matching visible stack entries for the name may contribute (most recent first; later entries fill property names not already set). If no matching visible entry exists, the result is undefined (nullish), not an empty object. qualifiers() returns an object whose properties are active qualifier names, each mapping to such a variables object; inactive names are omitted (never invented as empty objects).

Get (qualifier::name) and snapshots share the same stack and visibility rules: the most recent matching entry wins for a binding. Default snapshot visibility matches normal qualifier::name access in the current execution context. Optional includeUntrusted (default false) is only meaningful while the context is secure: set true so the snapshot includes the same frames you would see with qualifier::name if you were less secure (trusted and untrusted frames—not untrusted-only). When already not secure, true and false are the same because normal access already sees untrusted frames. Everyday qualifier::name access is unchanged and remains the hot path; snapshots are not intended for tight production loops.

Size warning: snapshot objects can get large. Qualifiers such as environment:: and request:: may contribute many properties, and some values can themselves be large. qualifiers() builds a nested object of full snapshots for every active qualifier name and multiplies that cost. Prefer qualifier::name for normal work; use qualifier() / qualifiers() sparingly, and avoid holding or repeatedly rebuilding large snapshots in long-running scripts.

Adaptive Models expose a rich current:: bag during on* hooks. The documented set for each hook is the property's contextType (for example modelGetObject or modelGetProperty on model object/property type definitions).
